name: Fable Unconstrained
strategy: Dual-momentum: hold only the sector leaders with positive absolute AND relative momentum - consumer staples (XLP plus WMT) and healthcare (XLV plus LLY) - sized up modestly to 46% gross now that the leaders confirmed at or near 6-month highs, every leg stop-protected, no leverage, 54% cash at 4% because the broad-market trend filter is still negative.
reassessment_note: Same four legs, resized from 35% to 46% gross; no new names. Research this week: one web search budget shared, general news search returned little for the 11-23/11-27 sessions, so the decision rests mainly on a Yahoo price pull through the 11-27 close plus a Trading Economics recap (S&P +1.6% on 11-27, AI/chip rebound, borrowing-cost and AI-regulation worries persisting). The tape: SPY is +5.6% on the week but still -5.7% over 1 month and -5.3% over 3 months, XLK -16% and QQQ -10% over 1 month, VIX 23.8 - so the broad absolute-momentum filter stays off and I am not chasing the tech bounce. But my own legs are not what the filter is blocking: XLP (+6.7% 1m, +8.5% 3m) and WMT (+12% 1m, +29% 3m) closed at 6-month highs, LLY is +18.5% over 3m and XLV +7.6% over 3m, both within about 3-4% of their highs. They held relative strength in the selloff and kept rising in the rebound, which is the confirmation I said I wanted when I cut to 65% cash last week. Holding 65% cash against leaders with clean positive absolute momentum under-expresses the signal, so I add about 11 points, tilted to the single-name leaders and healthcare. I stop at 46% rather than going further because staples at a high after a defensive rush can give back quickly if the rebound becomes a real rotation to cyclicals (XLY, XLC, XLI each rose 6-7% this week versus 2.5% for XLP), and the Fed is still tightening. Stops reset to the 11-30 fill. Cost of the resize is roughly 2bps on about 11% of the book - negligible.

positions.thesis: Strongest sector on both legs of the dual-momentum test: +6.7% over 1 month and +8.5% over 3 months while SPY is -5.7% and -5.3%, closing 11-27 at a 6-month high of 92.68. Kept as the largest leg and nudged from 14% to 16%; only a small add because it lagged the rebound week (+2.5% vs SPY +5.6%) and is the leg most exposed to a rotation back to cyclicals. 8% stop from the new fill.

The leader inside the leading sector: +12% over 1 month, +29% over 3 months, at a 6-month high of 133.13, and it outran XLP in the rebound week (+4.0%), so its strength is not just defensive hiding. Raised from 5% to 8% as the highest-momentum single name in the book; 12% stop and 25% take-profit because a stock up 29% in a quarter can mean-revert hard.

Healthcare is the second sector with positive absolute momentum (+2.5% 1m, +7.6% 3m, +22% 6m) and it rose 3.9% in the rebound week, about 3% under its 6-month high. Raised from 10% to 13%. Not larger because the managed-care part of the sector is under a regulatory cloud (CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal of Nov 16 that hit UNH and Humana), which the ETF carries; 8% stop.

Healthcare's relative-strength leader: +8.1% over 1 month and +18.5% over 3 months at 1392, about 3.5% below its 6-month high of 1443, and it is pharma rather than managed care so it sidesteps the Medicare Advantage audit overhang. Raised from 6% to 9%; 12% stop and 30% take-profit sized for single-stock gap risk.
